The details often left out

Six Sections Every Treatment Estimate Needs

A total without these details cannot be compared fairly. Ask the hospital to confirm each section in writing.

01

The exact clinical scope

Named procedure or treatment pathway, diagnosis used for the estimate, treating consultant, hospital campus and planned technique.

02

Tests before treatment

Consultations, imaging, pathology review, blood tests, pre-anaesthesia assessment and any test still required after arrival.

03

Professional and hospital fees

Surgeon or physician, anaesthesia, assisting specialists, theatre or procedure room, nursing, ICU and room category.

04

Implants, devices and medicines

Brand or specification where relevant, quantity, price ceiling, high-cost medicines, blood products and major consumables.

05

Expected stay and extension rates

Planned ICU and ward days, extra-day charges, companion arrangements and the expected time in India after discharge.

06

Exclusions and follow-up

Items outside the estimate, complication-related care, repeat procedures, rehabilitation, discharge medicines and follow-up consultations.

Compare properly
Make each hospital quote the same case

Compare Like for Like

Two estimates can look different because they are based on different assumptions. Align these fields before deciding that one hospital is cheaper.

CompareKeep this consistent
TreatmentSame diagnosis, procedure, technique and number of treatment cycles or sessions
HospitalExact campus, treating consultant and accreditation relevant to that location
Room and ICUSame room category and the same assumed number of ward and intensive-care days
Implant or deviceComparable specification, brand assumptions and replacement policy
MedicinesWhether routine and high-cost medicines are included, capped or excluded
AftercareFollow-up, rehabilitation, dressings, tests and medicines after discharge

Do not hide clinical information to obtain a lower figure. Missing reports, previous treatment or important medical conditions can make the estimate inaccurate and delay safe care.

Warning Signs in a Treatment Quote

One line only

A total is shown without the procedure, consultant, room or inclusions.

No clinical review

A fixed price is promised before anyone has read the reports.

Undefined implant

An implant or device is mentioned without a specification, limit or alternative.

No exclusions

The quote does not explain what happens if treatment or the stay changes.

Outcome guarantee

Success, cure, pregnancy or transplant approval is promised as certain.

Urgent payment pressure

You are pushed to transfer money before the provider and cancellation terms are clear.

Before payment

Five Checks Before Transferring Money

01

Match the beneficiary. Confirm the account belongs to the hospital or provider named in the estimate.

02

Reference the patient. Ask what patient name, hospital ID or estimate number to include.

03

Understand the deposit. Confirm which booking or clinical service the payment secures.

04

Read cancellation terms. Know which part is refundable if the visa, travel or treatment plan changes.

05

Keep the receipt. Save the transfer confirmation and obtain the provider’s acknowledgement.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a hospital estimate the same as a final bill?

No. An estimate is based on the information and assumptions available before treatment. The final bill reflects the care actually delivered, including any clinically necessary changes, additional tests or longer stay.

Should doctor fees be shown separately?

The quote should state whether the named consultant, assisting doctors, anaesthetist and other specialist fees are included. Separate line items are useful, but a package is acceptable when its scope is clear.

How should an implant be described?

Ask for the type, specification or expected brand, quantity and any price ceiling. Where the final choice depends on anatomy or availability, the hospital should explain how a more expensive option changes the total.

What does a package usually exclude?

Common exclusions can include unexpected ICU or room days, additional procedures, high-cost medicines, blood products, specialist consultations, complication-related care, rehabilitation and travel costs. The actual exclusions must be written by the hospital.

Should I pay the full amount before travelling?

Follow the hospital’s written payment policy. Confirm the receiving account, deposit purpose, refund or cancellation terms and receipt process before transferring money. Avoid personal accounts unless the hospital formally identifies one as authorised.

Can TIB HIND confirm whether a price is fair?

We can help organise the clinical scope and inclusions so estimates can be compared more accurately. We cannot determine clinical suitability or guarantee that a quoted figure will be the final bill.

What if one hospital quotes fewer days?

Ask why. A shorter expected stay may reflect a different technique, room assumption or clinical pathway. It can also make the total appear lower while leaving extra days outside the package.

Are flights, hotel and food part of a treatment package?

Usually they are separate unless the quote explicitly states otherwise. Budget visa fees, flights, accommodation outside hospital, meals, local transport and the companion’s costs independently.
